subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Which owner should claim or repair canonical literal `openai` auto session route state for doctor cleanup: the OpenAI provider contract, the Codex doctor contract, or a generic provider-agnostic auto-fallback repair?
rationale: The same `openai` id can represent canonical OpenAI provider use and the Codex app-server route, so changing ownership can either fix this drift or over-clear valid OpenAI session state.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and regression tests that clear stale auto fallback state without treating explicit user pins as stale.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI app-server route
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex route-state owner only if maintainers want Codex to own canonical OpenAI app-server session cleanup.

options.title: Use generic auto-fallback repair
options.body: Make doctor clear owner-independent auto overrides whose configured primary route no longer matches, while keeping user-selected overrides untouched.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and regression tests that clear stale auto fallback state without treating explicit user pins as stale.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current generic session-route repair and follow-up Codex stale-route fixes, so they have the clearest history for the owner-boundary decision.
